ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: FlowWorks
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Dig a channel and let a liquid flow into it. FlowWorks is one engine for everything liquid: canals, pits, ponds, tanks, hoses and rivers that move.
Digging. Mark ground and a colonist digs a canal there; dig the same ground again to go one level deeper. There are four depths, and the deepest is a pit. Trenches slow people down (deeper is slower, flooded is slower still, and a pit cannot be crossed), so a dug line is a real defensive barrier. A canal can be filled back in, and the liquid in it is pushed along rather than deleted. Digging sometimes turns up chunks of local stone or minerals, with a letter the first time each one appears.
Flow. Any pond is a source: liquid spreads along a canal dug from its edge in steady pulses and stays inside the dug channel. A lake touching the map edge never runs dry; an enclosed pond visibly shrinks as it pays out and slowly refills from rain, season and seepage. Rain fills open trenches while roofed ones stay dry, and a canal that runs off the map edge drains away. Each liquid keeps its own nature (tar crawls while water runs), and two different liquids never mix: where their fronts meet, both stop. Canyon floods run through your canals instead of wiping them out.
Fire. Fire or an explosion lights tar, oil or propane, and the flame travels along the canal like a fuse you can outrun. A burning canal burns for days, spreads back into its pond and sets anyone standing in it alight. Firefoam puts it out, and rain has a chance to. Corrosive liquids can eat whatever stands in them (off by default).
Pits. Anything that falls into a pit at least as wide as it is cannot climb out; a creature too wide for the pit simply walks out. Colonists never walk into an open pit; being pushed in or jumping in on purpose is what puts someone down there, and the fall hurts. Someone in a pit can only trade fire with whoever stands at its edge. A pit cover hides the hole and gives way underfoot (three builds bear different weights), spikes at the bottom wound whoever falls on them, and opening a gate floods an occupied pit to drown, poison or burn whoever is in it. Lower a ladder and people climb out; raise it and they are stranded. Wall a pit in and add a prisoner bed and it becomes a prison wardens run from the lip; an open pit bakes by day and freezes by night, wearing down a prisoner's resistance. Sluice gates and security grates let liquid through but hold creatures and prisoners.
Carry and store. Bottles, buckets and barrels fill at a matching shore or tank and wash out for reuse. Tanks hold a bulk stock of one liquid at a time, pumps move liquid out of ponds and canals, and hose reels (moved here from Gimme Some Slack) lay a hose a colonist carries out and winds back, lying flat when empty and plumping while liquid flows, with relay reels to reach further and four looks to pick from on the build button. Drills and taps bring underground liquids up, cleaned water feeds thirst, and ruined industrial liquid plants (desalination, tar refinery, pumping station) can be found and repaired.
The land. Many liquids exist as ground (brine, boiling water, propane, acid, tar and more), each with its own terrain. Newly generated maps get shores of the local liquid, and hot rivers steam in colour. On the planet map, rivers run red at their headwaters, brackish green-brown through the jungle and a toxic brown-blue at their dead ends. A swale turns nearby sand into soil while water stands in it. Rivers move: the current shoves pawns, corpses and loose items downstream, and anyone swept off the map edge walks home a few days later. Ford stones, weirs that catch fish and calm the water upstream, bank stakes that hold back a spring flood, and ferry ropes let you work with the river rather than around it. Pan a river for gold, or set a sluice box to sift ore from a stream.
Every mechanic has a switch in Mod Settings; with everything off, the mod still digs dry canals.
Requires Harmony and all five RimWorld expansions.
